observation.visible_scene: An outdoor scene under a pale overcast sky. In the foreground a low dirt berm with a fence line runs across the bottom; at right stands a wooden utility pole with a street lamp, and at bottom-right a gray electrical cabinet on a white base. The center-left is dominated by a large billowing fireball: bright orange-yellow flames embedded in a cauliflower-like mass of dark smoke, with an orange smoke plume rising above it. To the left is a separate, fainter grayish-brown smoke cloud, and to the right a thin orange arcing streak (smoke/fire trail) crosses the sky. The fireball is already fully developed and burning at the first frame.
visible_changes: The luminous flame core within the fireball shifts upward through the dark smoke mass over the excerpt, and the overall cloud column expands vertically while the orange plume above it grows taller and more diffuse.
The left grayish smoke cloud slowly broadens and its edges soften as the segment progresses.
The right orange arcing streak remains present and roughly constant in shape throughout.

The utility pole, street lamp and electrical box change their pixel positions frame-to-frame (and one frame is motion-blurred), indicating slight handheld camera shake/pan rather than movement of those objects; the fireball's position relative to the pole also shifts accordingly.
The fireball's internal bright patches flicker in intensity between frames (combustion variability), not a single steady glow.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or nature of the burning material, and any preceding ignition event.
Whether the fire continues, diminishes, or is extinguished after the last frame.
The true start of the fireball, since it is already mid-burn at t=0.
uncertain_details: Whether the apparent upward drift of the flame core is partly a camera tilt versus genuine rising of hot gases.
Whether the left gray plume translates with wind or merely expands in place.
The identity of the right orange streak (smoke trail vs. burning line).
The exact magnitude of camera pan/zoom versus object motion, given the small frame-to-frame shifts.
